I built the LaTeX skeleton, the macros, the bibliography and the label conventions in /workspace/minlp-notes/paper-open-minlplib. `latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode main.tex` exits with status 0 and writes a 4-page `build/main.pdf`. The log has no LaTeX errors. The only warnings are the intended `\TODO` and `\archiveDOI` placeholder warnings, plus the empty-bibliography notice from natbib. BibTeX also reports "no \citation commands"; this goes away with the first citation and did not fail the build. All of this is uncommitted.

**main.tex**
- `article` 11pt, A4, 25 mm margins. Packages: T1/lmodern, amsmath, amssymb, amsthm, mathtools, booktabs, longtable, graphicx, xcolor, tcolorbox, microtype, natbib (round, `plainnat`), xurl, hyperref and cleveref (capitalise, noabbrev, nameinlink). siunitx is not installed on this machine, so the `\sci` macro replaces it.
- Title from the outline, empty author.
- Input order follows the outline. The bibliography comes after Section 11, then `\appendix`.

**Section stubs**
- 31 files in `sections/`. Each has its `\section` title, the requested label and a red `\TODO`.
- The main-text stubs also contain the outline's subsections with labels (for example `sec:semantics-display`), so writers can cross-reference each other's parts before the text exists.
- I added one file you did not list: `sections/B0-families.tex`, containing the section "Certificates by family" (`app:families`). Files B1–B9 open with `\subsection`, so the lettering matches the outline: A, B.1–B.9, C–J.
- `11-conclusion.tex` ends with an unnumbered "Statements and declarations" stub. It contains no AI-use statement (decision D7).

**macros.tex**
- Theorem-like environments on one counter numbered by section. A lemma is still referenced as "Lemma", which I checked in a test document.
- A tagged `hypothesis` environment for (H) and (H0).
- A breakable `certbox` and a numbered `infobox` ("Box n").
- `\inst`, which handles underscores, breaks lines only after `_` or `-`, and works in titles and PDF bookmarks.
- The notation macros, `\sci`, `\TODO` and `\archiveDOI`.

**references.bib** has 147 entries, all ASCII.
- It covers all 138 slugs in outline section 7 and the 7 further slugs cited in L1–L3.
- Two entries have no KB package: `vigerske2014-minlplib-2` (the MAGO 2014 paper "MINLPLib 2", pp. 137–140) and `zimmerman2011-matpower-steady-state-operations-planning` (the paper MATPOWER asks users of its case data to cite).
- BibTeX on a `\nocite{*}` test document read all 147 entries with no warnings and no errors.
- I checked journal metadata against Crossref and arXiv and fixed several clear errors in the KB data:
  - **josz2015:** the KB title was wrong. The paper is "Application of the Moment–SOS Approach to Global Optimization of the OPF Problem", IEEE TPWRS 30(1), 2015.
  - **bingane2019:** title and venue were wrong. It is "Tight-and-cheap conic relaxation for the AC optimal power flow problem", IEEE TPWRS 33(6), 2018.
  - **coffrin2014:** wrong title expansion and author first names.
  - **Wrong author names:** ambrosio2015, gleixner2012, oustry2022, peyrl2008, schweidtmann2019, tessier2000, najman2021, the Göß et al. 2026 paper ("Martin", not "Martín"), shcherbina0000, ghezzi2026 (Andrea, not Riccardo) and the Karia Zenodo record.
  - **Published versions instead of preprints:** anderson2018, bertsimas2025, tasseff2022, mcdonald1995.
  - **Missing volumes and pages** filled in for many journal entries.
- Web resources (MINLPLib, QPLIB, the Mittelmann pages, CAMINO, Zenodo and others) are `@misc` entries with URL and access date.

**development/labels.md** lists:
- every section and subsection label;
- the label convention and family short names;
- the outline's theorem, table, figure and box numbering mapped to planned labels;
- the macro and environment reference with a certificate-box template;
- the bibliography notes, including the corrections above.

Two other small files: `latexmkrc` (sends output to `build/`) and `.gitignore` (ignores `build/`). Nothing under `R/` or `literature/` was edited, and no scientific scripts were run.
